questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Depending on your faculty and classes, there might be substantial transportation time

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We had signed up for university housing for the first three weeks  - during an introductory language course - but were told upon arrival that they had somehow missed us. Highly disappointing, as we had to live in a hotel for three nights, despite the fact that the university housing was not full. This experience was characterised by employees and university representatives spending more time on explaining why our problem was not covered by their area of work, rather than helping us solve the issue and figure out whether we could have a roof over our heads

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While the process itself was easy albeit stressful, there were little information beforehand. Course registration happen after arrival, which make it difficult to plan when your home university requires you to cover certain mandatory classes. Several of my fellow students and I even experienced that, a week after the semester started, a class that we had already been approved for by the host university was suddenly not available to us anymore. As the enrollment period is simultaneous with the beginning of the semester and many students are on waiting list for some classes for at least a few days, you cannot be certain of which classes to attend for the first week.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration happen after arrival and the enrollment period is simultaneous with the beginning of the semester. Registration happens online, but much e-mail correspondence with the International Office is needed, as the system is not build for exchange students. Some classes are off limits in the system but are available for exchange students, and vice versa

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very, a class that was supposed to cover two classes required by my home university was suddenly not available after arrival, with the explanation that they forgot to change it in the system. However, several student from my home university had put this class in their pre-approval, so it seemed strange that the university had approved all these students without noticing that the class was not available

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have mandatory classes at your home university I would recommend to find two-to-three options, as some classes might not be available or that you end up on the waiting list for a certain class

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Much of the teaching has been unstructured with no clear guidelines for what is expected for exams, participation etc., and with either little connection betweeen the syllabus and the teaching or with the lecture being a summary of the syllabus.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As the BA classes covered topics that my home university covered during the first three semesters I have mainly attended MA classes where the academic level has been okay

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: To me it seemed unstructured with little overview or connection across syllabus and topics - no time were spent on relating the texts in the syllabus to each other and to thus clarify differences and similarities between theories/authors/approaches in the various topics covered in a semester

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you're going to Prague for the parties you should know that the vibe at the 'mainstream' clubs is more A-bar than Søpavillionen - check the instagram of Duplex or One Club, that gives a pretty good picture of how most clubs are in Prague
The academic level is not comparable and the uni here is less strict with deadlines but also slower with giving out information, compared to KU. Whether that's positive or negative is up to you.
On a more general note, scandinavians seem to be a few years older than other exchange students, who can seem a bit high-school-y at times. Again, whether that's positive or negative is up to you

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settling in and accepting that my expectations might have been to high
